races.name: Sky Sports Racing Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Elated
runners_data.note: Consistent placer for Ben Pauling but has finished third in five of her last six outings — win-shy profile, Good ground is fine, runs in hood (hg:p), and the step up to 2m1f may suit but a lack of early speed limits upside.|

runners_data.name: Getmyfriend
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton combination is firing at 10/26 over 14 days; already won on Good ground over hurdles, sits at OR 120, and the prominent style means she can track For Her Glory without over-extending — clear first-choice challenger.|

runners_data.name: Winters Hill
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a noted tendency to fade in the finish — three consecutive finishes of 7th or 8th paint a worrying picture, and despite Good ground being fine on paper, the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 1/16 adds further caution.|

runners_data.name: For Her Glory
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner with a win already on Good ground at 16f; Sean Bowen is one of the strongest jockeys in the field, Olly Murphy's stable is in reasonable form, and uncontested lead-setting at this trip on Good turf is exactly where she is most dangerous.|

runners_data.name: Likewhatyousee
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr takes the ride for the family yard; placed on Good ground previously and the prominent style means she will position close to the pace — limited experience over hurdles but flat form over shorter suggests ability is there.|

runners_data.name: Lundy View
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and twice finished 6th or 7th on Good ground at 17f — the experience deficit is real, trainer Nigel Hawke has a modest 14-day strike rate of 1/3, and the unknown style (U) means this runner is essentially an unknown quantity in a tactical race.|

runners_data.name: Princess Of Ballea
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with multiple placed efforts on Good ground across varying distances; Harry Reed takes the ride for Daisy Hitchins whose stable is quiet (0/1, 14 days), and she needs a strong gallop to pounce late — one For Her Glory may not provide.|

runners_data.name: Steal A Glance
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies partners this Anthony Honeyball runner who has placed on Good ground in a prominent style; wears tongue-tie (hg:t), trainer is cold at 0/3 over 14 days, and a disappointing 9th last time out makes it hard to be confident.|

races.paceDynamic: For Her Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Sean Bowen aboard for Olly Murphy, she is expected to establish a clear lead and control tempo from the outset at a measured, sustainable gallop over 2m1f on Good ground. Getmyfriend, Likewhatyousee, and Steal A Glance all carry prominent-running profiles and will sit in behind, but none appears likely to seriously challenge For Her Glory for the lead, meaning the pace should remain honest rather than punishing. Winters Hill and Princess Of Ballea are hold-up types who will need the race to come back to them in the straight, though Winters Hill's noted tendency to fade late is a concern in that context. This shape — one uncontested front-runner setting a fair but not scorching tempo — classically favours prominent racers who can track the leader economically and pounce in the straight, rather than deep hold-up horses who need a truly strong gallop to set up a late run.

scenarios.title: Front-Runner Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If For Her Glory dictates an uncontested, measured pace and her rivals fail to reel her in turning for home.
scenarios.body: If For Her Glory dictates an uncontested, measured pace and her rivals fail to reel her in turning for home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent tracker stalks For Her Glory throughout and has enough in reserve to overtake in the final flight.
scenarios.body: If a prominent tracker stalks For Her Glory throughout and has enough in reserve to overtake in the final flight.

scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final mile and hold-up horses get into contention via a sustained staying finish.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the final mile and hold-up horses get into contention via a sustained staying finish.

scenarios.title: Muddle and Upset

watchPoints.text: For Her Glory (Sean Bowen) has a clear lead from the outset and no obvious challenger — watch whether the prominent trio of Getmyfriend, Likewhatyousee, and Steal A Glance can collectively apply enough pressure to bring her back, or whether she simply pings the last and wins unchallenged.

Winters Hill is flagged as a fader in the finish — if Callum Pritchard attempts to improve from off the pace and cannot sustain her effort over the final two flights, she could cause interference or hamper runners coming through on her inner.

Getmyfriend's last run was 38 days ago — watch in the paddock and early in the race for signs of freshness or over-enthusiasm from Harry Skelton's partner that could see her burn petrol too early while tracking the leader.

Lundy View (James Davies) has run only twice and both runs were over 17f on Good ground — this 2m1f trip is a slight shortening and the lightly-raced tag means she could produce an unexpected performance in either direction.

Elated has finished third in five of her last six — watch whether Ben Pauling's runner finally converts under Ben Jones on a track and trip she has not previously encountered, or whether the pattern of placing without winning continues.

races.name: Sun Racing Free Tickets With Sun Club Novices' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kittys Glance
runners_data.note: Alan King's five-year-old owns the race record that matters most here — three consecutive runs at Newton Abbot on Good ground including a win at 20f — and maps as the lone front-runner, so she will control fractions entirely unopposed; the concern is whether a 22-day turnaround and 168lbs tests her stamina, but her style fit is outstanding.

runners_data.name: Backer Bilk
runners_data.note: Nick Slatter's claim is a useful weight-saving angle for a hold-up horse who has placed at 16f on Good ground twice recently, and at OR 98 he has the highest rating among the chasers; the step up to 2m2½f from a 2m base is an open question, and 45 days off the track makes fitness worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Ask Peter
runners_data.note: Anthony Honeyball's seven-year-old is a hold-up type with two placing efforts on Good going in his recent history and wears a tongue-tie; the 10lb claimer James Robottom reduces the burden to 147lbs, and a recent run 21 days ago suggests he arrives in decent order, though his trainer's 0-from-3 in the last 14 days is a mild negative.

runners_data.name: Adaay Dancing
runners_data.note: Max Comley's five-year-old is genuinely a hold-up horse by nature, though with so many similar types in this field he is likely to be shuffled forward from his preferred rear position into a midfield spot that doesn't suit; his going form shows only 7 wins/places from 15 comparable efforts, and a 45-day break adds doubt.

runners_data.name: Hawa Jumeirah
runners_data.note: Helen Nelmes has had no runners in the last 14 days, so there is limited live-trainer intelligence here; Hawa Jumeirah is a natural hold-up operator who has finished 5th or worse in all five recent starts, and the redistribution into midfield will not help a horse whose best chance depends on being produced late from the back.

runners_data.name: Saucats
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's five-year-old has run 13 of his last 15 starts on Good going, making the surface entirely familiar, and his most recent run came only 10 days ago suggesting he arrives fit; while he is another true hold-up type forced into a midfield mapping by field congestion, his consistent placing efforts (three in last five) and course-proven stamina over this trip make him the most reliable hold-up type in the field.

runners_data.name: Katzoff
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's nine-year-old is a non-runner as flagged in the data, so his participation should be confirmed before any assessment is applied; on paper he has 14 Good-going runs in his history and a single placing, suggesting the surface has not brought out the best of him, and his last run was just three days ago.

races.paceDynamic: Kittys Glance is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner novice handicap hurdle and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate an uncontested, measured gallop over the 2m2½f trip on Good ground at Newton Abbot. Alan King's five-year-old has won and placed at this distance on Good going and will control fractions entirely on her own terms, meaning the pace is unlikely to be severe enough to string the field out early. The rest of the field — Backer Bilk, Ask Peter, Adaay Dancing, Hawa Jumeirah, Saucats, and Katzoff — are all natural hold-up or midfield types, but with five genuine hold-up horses competing for the same rear-ground, not all can settle in their preferred position; Adaay Dancing and Hawa Jumeirah are the most likely to be forced forward against their natural style, while Backer Bilk and Ask Peter may genuinely get cover off the pace. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a sustainable, controlled pace — strongly favours hold-up horses with a genuine late kick, provided the tempo is not so slow it degenerates into a sprint, and Kittys Glance's ability to control the race makes her own chance from just off the lead formidable.

scenarios.title: Kittys Glance Dictates Unchallenged

scenarios.body: If Kittys Glance leads throughout at a controlled pace and the hold-up horses fail to generate sufficient momentum from the rear to reel her in.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to stretch the field and one of the genuine hold-up horses produces a powerful late run to collar Kittys Glance at the last.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just fast enough to stretch the field and one of the genuine hold-up horses produces a powerful late run to collar Kittys Glance at the last.

scenarios.trigger: If Kittys Glance sets an unusually slow tempo, turning the race into a flat-out dash from the home turn.

scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Threads Through

watchPoints.text: Kittys Glance — if she jumps cleanly at the first two hurdles and establishes an uncontested lead, Tom Bellamy will have fully dictated the race; watch whether any rival attempts to go with her, as truly unchallenged the race is hers to lose.

Backer Bilk — Nick Slatter (3lb claimer) has placed twice on Good going at a shorter trip; watch whether he travels smoothly in the early stages, as his ability to get cover behind the leader will be crucial if he is to deliver a late challenge.

Saucats — 10 days since last run is very tight, but his trainer had a winner in the past 14 days and his Good-going fitness is the best-evidenced in the field; watch his jumping — if he pings hurdles in the back straight he may close faster than his OR 79 suggests.
Katzoff — listed as a non-runner; racecourse confirmation of his participation or absence will change the pace map and runner count, and bettors should verify before the off.

Adaay Dancing and Hawa Jumeirah — both true hold-up types likely forced into midfield by field congestion; watch early to see whether either attempts to drop out to the rear regardless, as that will create further bunching and potential traffic issues turning for home.

races.name: St. Austell Brewery Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Northern Symphonie
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with solid course-distance form at Newton Abbot (3rd over 2m, 5th over 2m4f on Good), giving her the best contextual profile among the chasers; Megan Bevan's 7lb claim reduces her already competitive 168lbs burden and her trainer Harriet Dickin's flat 0/5 in the 14-day window is worth noting as a mild dampener — she will need Miss Kassiopi to do her a favour late on.

runners_data.name: Miss Kassiopi
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in this race and the clear pace-controlling asset; Harry Skelton's booking for an in-form Dan Skelton yard (13/29 in 14 days) is a significant positive flag, and her recent form of 2-1-3 demonstrates consistency at this sort of mark — the STYLE_FIT tag noting she's racing out of natural role is less relevant here because she IS the lone pace-setter, meaning she will secure her natural position regardless.

runners_data.name: Hurst Hill
runners_data.note: Staying type with a decent second over 2m4f on Good last time at this venue for Seamus Mullins; Daniel Sansom's 3lb claim helps at 156lbs and her pattern of running on from off the pace suits this race shape — but she has been placed just once in five starts and needs the pace to be genuinely searching for her staying profile to overhaul a fresh front-runner.

runners_data.name: Global Hideaway
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a string of modest efforts at shorter trips (all five recent runs at 2m or under), so this 2m5½f trip on Good is uncharted stamina territory; naturally a hold-up runner, she has been mapped to midfield because the field is saturated with similar types — her form figures of 9-8-4-4 suggest she rarely gets involved at the business end and her experience at this trip is nil.

runners_data.name: Blue Siam
runners_data.note: Four-year-old wearing a visor for the first time, running for handler Syd Hosie who has had no winners from four runners in the 14-day window; her form figures are a string of mid-pack finishes at shorter trips and, though young horses can improve quickly, her redistribution from hold-up to midfield reflects a race where she will struggle to find her natural rhythm off a potentially slow pace.

runners_data.name: Ghost Jury
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Sean Bowen — one of the best judge-of-pace jockeys in the sport — with five recent runs all on Good ground and a recent first and second in form (U4-125); she has been pushed into midfield on the map because the rear is crowded with hold-up types, but Bowen's tactical nous means she could still get a clear passage late if the race sets up at all — trainer Kayley Woollacott has a quiet yard right now (0/1 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Bee's Kiss
runners_data.note: Modest form string of P097-P including a pulled-up last time for Jimmy Frost; wearing a hood, she has struggled to complete and show any meaningful form recently, with only three of six recent runs resulting in a finish — this 2m5½f trip is her longest for some time and the combination of jumping fragility and low form make her the most speculative runner in the field.

runners_data.name: At Sunrise
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner; included for completeness — a hold-up type for David Weston whose best form has come over slightly shorter trips on Good ground, but her absence reduces the field to seven and eliminates one more horse competing for hold-up running room at the rear.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Kassiopi is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and, with Harry Skelton aboard for a in-form yard, she is likely to be allowed to stride into an uncontested lead from the outset over this 2m5½f trip on Good ground at Newton Abbot. The remainder of the field — Northern Symphonie, Hurst Hill, Global Hideaway, Blue Siam, Ghost Jury, Bee's Kiss, and At Sunrise (non-runner) — are all natural hold-up or midfield types, meaning the pace Miss Kassiopi sets will be controlled and unhurried rather than pressured. This creates a scenario where she dictates every yard, conserves energy over the longer trip, and potentially kicks clear at her own discretion in the straight. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can legitimately place at the rear; Global Hideaway, Blue Siam, Ghost Jury, and Bee's Kiss have all been redistributed to midfield, but in reality several of them will be tracking in a bunch some way off the leader — true hold-up running will be difficult to execute cleanly from that compressed group. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: a lone front-runner dictating a sustainable gallop on Good ground over an extended trip strongly favours a horse who leads and travels fluently, with hold-up horses needing a strong pace to close into — which this race shape is unlikely to generate.

scenarios.title: Kassiopi Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Kassiopi is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a measured, accurate gallop that the hold-up pack cannot close.
scenarios.body: If Miss Kassiopi is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a measured, accurate gallop that the hold-up pack cannot close.

scenarios.body: If the pack tracks Miss Kassiopi at a tighter margin than expected and the cumulative effect of jumping 17 hurdles in front takes its toll in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively strong enough to burn off the mid-packers and one of the genuinely patient hold-up types gets a clear run to unleash a late challenge.
scenarios.body: If the pace is deceptively strong enough to burn off the mid-packers and one of the genuinely patient hold-up types gets a clear run to unleash a late challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Kassiopi makes a critical jumping error or is taken on unexpectedly early, creating a stop-start gallop that turns the race into a flat-footed sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If Miss Kassiopi makes a critical jumping error or is taken on unexpectedly early, creating a stop-start gallop that turns the race into a flat-footed sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Miss Kassiopi and Harry Skelton — watch whether she jumps cleanly at the first three hurdles; any blunder could compromise her lead and hand momentum to the chasing pack, fundamentally altering the entire race shape.

The compressed midfield cluster of Global Hideaway, Blue Siam, Ghost Jury, and Bee's Kiss — all natural hold-up horses forced into a midfield bunch — creates significant risk of interference, checked runs, and hampered jumps from the third hurdle onward; Sean Bowen on Ghost Jury will need a clean passage.

Northern Symphonie's headgear (blinkers) could see her race more keenly than usual and drift closer to Miss Kassiopi earlier than her hold-up style dictates, potentially bridging the gap sooner — watch how Megan Bevan manages her position in the first mile.

Hurst Hill's trainer Seamus Mullins has had no winners from three runners in the last 14 days — a stable running below par is worth factoring into any assessment of whether this horse arrives at the race in optimal condition.

Good ground is confirmed across all six Newton Abbot races today with no sectional variation reported — no surface concern for any runner, but this consistency means Miss Kassiopi's front-running advantage is fully intact with no chance of deterioration helping the hold-up horses.

races.name: Howden Insurance Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Duke Of Luckley
runners_data.note: Trainer Martin Keighley wins at just 1/6 in the past 14 days and this 9-year-old bounced back to winning form last time (31 days ago) on Good ground over the same 16f trip, giving him an ideal profile for front-running on a course where his Good-ground record reads 14 runs, 5 wins, 8 places; Freddie Keighley's 5lb claim is a potential asset on a horse that jumps cleanly and controls its own destiny, though his style-fit rating of 0.92 reflects he is fractionally off his ideal tactical slot here.

runners_data.name: Krak
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners this 6-year-old for the Twiston-Davies team (0/5 in the last 14 days, which tempers expectations) whose last two runs over 16f on Good were a runner-up and a third, suggesting the combination of trip and going suits well; 48 days off the track is not a concern for this yard, and his profile as a prominent tracker fits the predicted race shape more naturally than any rival here.

runners_data.name: Schmilsson
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy has been in solid recent form (5/12 in 14 days) and Sean Bowen is a high-class booking, but 343 days off the track is a significant fitness question for this 6-year-old; by nature a front-runner or prominent racer, the crowded pace positions in this field mean he is forced back from his ideal berth, and his style-fit tag of 0.93 — combined with an extended absence — makes his chance hard to assess with confidence even though his form includes two wins over this exact course and distance.

runners_data.name: Gore Point
runners_data.note: Anthony Honeyball's 6-year-old ran just four days ago, and that quick turnaround is the headline concern here regardless of anything else; a natural prominent racer whose place in the field structure has been shifted rearward because there is simply no room for another horse at the front, his Good-ground record (10 runs, 3 wins, 8 places at 15 runs sim-going) is genuinely solid, but Sam Twiston-Davies will need to manage the horse's energy after such a rapid return.

races.paceDynamic: Duke Of Luckley is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only four runners, is almost certain to bowl along at the head of affairs from the outset, setting a tempo that he controls entirely on his own terms. Krak is the most natural challenger for an early prominent position, tracking Duke Of Luckley through the first half of the race, while Schmilsson — a genuine prominent type — will be unable to secure that berth naturally and is likely to be shuffled back, racing in a position that does not suit his style. This field holds more prominent-minded horses than can realistically secure those positions: Duke Of Luckley and Krak are best placed to get the ground they want, while Schmilsson and Gore Point are effectively mapped away from their natural slots. A controlled, front-runner-dominated pace over 2m½f on Good ground at Newton Abbot heavily favours a prominent tracker who can sit within a length or two of the leader, travel comfortably, and pick up from the second-last — making Krak's profile the most tactically advantaged in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Duke Of Luckley's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the single biggest variable — if he finds an uncontested rhythm, he becomes very hard to dislodge and the whole race shape pivots around his jumping accuracy.

Schmilsson's 343-day absence means race-fitness is unproven; if he blows up in the final half-mile after initially tracking nearer the pace than his mapped position suggests, the race order could change dramatically from the last fence.

Gore Point ran only four days ago — watch the betting market and early behavioural signs in the paddock for any indication that the quick turnaround has taken a physical toll before the race even begins.

With only four runners, a single jumping error or exit will dramatically thin the field; Krak has mixed jumping form (unseated and pulled up on recent starts) which could prove decisive if it recurs in a race with no margin for error.

Harry Skelton and Sean Bowen are both high-profile bookings in a small field — if their market moves are divergent approaching post-time, that could signal inside knowledge about relative freshness or schooling form that is not captured in the public record.

races.name: Gordon Rowe Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Charlus
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by Dan Skelton with Harry Skelton aboard — a formidable combination — but returning after 84 days off with a recent form string of F-P-0-P that screams unreliability, and a specific note that it fades in the finish undermines its hold-up profile badly on what should be Good ground that suits it.

runners_data.name: Continuance
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and the pace-maker here; Good ground suits with a sim-going record of 2W4P, but the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.91 is academic given it will almost certainly lead — the real question is whether its 166lbs and OR 122 allow it to sustain the gallop to the finish with a 5-year-old's residual stamina.

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: Prominent racer under Brian Hughes who has recorded three wins from 11 starts on similar going and won over 16f on Good ground before; the unexplained 75-day absence with a Flat run flag (15F) warrants monitoring, but he should be close enough to pounce if Continuance weakens.

runners_data.name: Arctic Voyage
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who has won two of six starts on Good ground over 16-17f and arrives on a sharp 30-day turnaround in excellent form (3P1-12); the 4-year-old is the lightest weight in the field at 152lbs, which is a meaningful pull at the weights, and the Good surface is precisely what its record demands.

runners_data.name: Emerald Time
runners_data.note: A true rear-of-field horse whose natural position is at the back, though the congested hold-up group means it is likely to race further forward than ideal — that style displacement, flagged with a STYLE_FIT of 0.90, reduces its chance of landing a telling blow; recent form of 1-5-6-7 is a mixed picture and the hg:t headgear note may indicate a horse that needs specific conditions to fire.

races.paceDynamic: Continuance is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners in a 2m1f handicap hurdle on Good ground at Newton Abbot, is likely to set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without meaningful pressure. Max Of Stars is also a prominent-racing type and will likely track Continuance closely, meaning the pace should be honest enough without becoming a true test of stamina. Arctic Voyage and Charlus are both hold-up horses who will need this pair to set enough froth to reel in, while Emerald Time — a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield in the map because the rear is more congested than it appears — will be ridden to get cover rather than its natural position at the tail of the field. This race shape, with a controlled front-runner and a prominent stalker, classically favours the patient hold-up horse who can pick off tiring rivals in the final two flights, provided the pace is sufficient — Arctic Voyage, with a record of winning prominently-run races on Good ground and a strong recent profile, sits in the sweet spot, while Charlus carries a stamina concern that undermines its hold-up profile.

watchPoints.text: Charlus is 84 days fresh with poor recent form and a noted tendency to fade — if it mis-jumps or stops quickly from two out it could impede Arctic Voyage or Emerald Time closing from behind.

Emerald Time is a genuine hold-up horse forced into a more prominent position by the field makeup — watch whether Tom Bellamy can settle it in its natural rhythm early or whether it races too keenly and empties in the straight.

Max Of Stars carries a Flat run (15F) flag after 75 days off — Brian Hughes will know its fitness level but a stamina question over 2m1f after that background is live, and a sudden fade from the front two would dramatically alter the race shape.

Continuance's apprentice rider Freddie Keighley (5lb claimer) could be a factor in how the pace is managed — a greener front-running ride risks either going too fast too soon or failing to kick when it matters, which shapes the entire race.

With only five runners on a right-handed Newton Abbot track, the race is unlikely to get strong early, meaning hold-up horses may need to be more aggressive from three out than their jockeys ideally want — a key tactical moment to watch at the top of the hill.

races.name: William Hill Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Great d'Ange
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old hold-up performer returning after 34 days, sporting tongue-tie, with strong similar-going credentials (13/15) and placed efforts over this sort of trip on Good; the key question is whether the pace is strong enough to set up his late run at 3m2f.

runners_data.name: Winning Paddy
runners_data.note: Has winning form at this course and distance on Good ground and his similar-going record (4/5) is excellent, but his last four runs include a string of defeats and at OR=94 he carries a penalty that will test his resolve over the final fence.

runners_data.name: Longhouse Star
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride on a horse returning from a 676-day absence — that layoff is the dominant concern here, and though he has been fitted with a tongue-piece and a pad, his true style is a deep hold-up finisher who tends to fade late, making a rusty comeback at 3m2f a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Mcgregors Charge
runners_data.note: A naturally patient hold-up horse in effect forced to race closer to the pace than he would ideally like given the redistribution in this field; his recent form includes consecutive pulled-ups and his similar-going record over this sort of ground (10/15) offers only modest encouragement.

runners_data.name: Daring Plan
runners_data.note: Arrives on the back of a recent win (20 days ago) and her form figures include placed efforts at this sort of trip, though Lucy Gardner's ride and a true hold-up style that the race shape may not accommodate makes this harder than the win suggests.

runners_data.name: He Is A Cracker
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner who sets the entire tactical agenda; his jumping reliability and how well claimer Isabelle Ryder manages the tempo over 3m2f are pivotal, and his 194-day absence from competition is a notable fitness query on top of his STYLE_FIT tag.

runners_data.name: Blackacre
runners_data.note: A young seven-year-old chaser who is naturally a hold-up type but will likely find himself in a midfield position, his form includes a fall and his visor headgear suggests he needs visual encouragement; similar-going figures (7/15) are only average.

runners_data.name: Radharc Na Slaine
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes over on a horse who ran just seven days ago and has excellent similar-going form (13/15 with a win); his prominent style is a natural fit to track He Is A Cracker throughout and he is the horse best positioned to capitalise if the leader weakens.

races.paceDynamic: He Is A Cracker is the lone confirmed front-runner and, ridden by claimer Isabelle Ryder, will set out to control this 3m2f chase from the front at what should be a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good ground. Radharc Na Slaine is the only other horse with genuine prominent tendencies and Sean Bowen is capable of tracking up closely, meaning the early order is relatively settled rather than a battle for the lead. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can be accommodated at the rear — Longhouse Star, Mcgregors Charge, Daring Plan and Blackacre are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to a midfield mapping, but in practice they cannot all sit as deep as they would wish, and several will be forced to race closer than ideal. This controlled, single-setter shape over a stamina-demanding 3m2f strongly favours horses with genuine staying power who can travel prominently or make smooth headway from a genuine midfield position — chasers who relish the stamina test and can quicken off a steady fractions race rather than those who depend on being produced late from the back.

watchPoints.text: He Is A Cracker's jumping — any mistake on the front end under claimer Isabelle Ryder could immediately reorder this entire race, as there is no other natural leader to take over.

Longhouse Star's racecourse fitness after 676 days absent is a major unknown; Harry Skelton may have to nurse him through the early stages, and a stopping run could become a traffic hazard for hold-up horses tracking behind.

Radharc Na Slaine ran just seven days ago — monitor his demeanour in the paddock and at the start, as a horse returning so quickly on Good ground over 3m2f will be tested on residual fatigue in the closing stages.

Several hold-up horses (Mcgregors Charge, Daring Plan, Blackacre) will jostle for midfield positions on the first circuit — watch for early crowding or interference approaching the first few fences that could unsettle any of them.

Great d'Ange is equipped with a tongue-tie and has the strongest profile of the genuine late-finishers; if the front end does not dominate, watch whether Tom Broughton (3) can find a clear passage from the home turn.
